title: Canonical determinant section of a rank-zero two-term perfect object
statement:
Let $V$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $K\in D(\mathcal O_V)$ [def-pc-derived-category] a perfect object [def-pc-perfect-complex] of Tor amplitude $[0,1]$: derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] with any module has cohomology only in these two degrees. Suppose $K$ has virtual rank zero, meaning that each local model $[E^0\xrightarrow d E^1]$ in degrees $0,1$ has equal finite locally free ranks [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. There is a functorial pair $(D(K),\delta_K)$ consisting of an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] and a global section, with canonical local identifications
$$(D(K),\delta_K)\simeq(\det E^1\otimes(\det E^0)^{-1},\det d),$$
where $\det E=\bigwedge^{\operatorname{rk}E}E$ [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. Derived isomorphisms induce isomorphisms of pairs, independently of the model, preserving identities and composition. For every scheme map $h:V'\to V$ the pair for $Lh^*K$ is canonically $h^*(D(K),\delta_K)$ [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-module-pullback], compatibly with derived isomorphisms, identities and composition. For every invertible module $N$ on $V$ there is a canonical identification of pairs for $K\otimes N$ and $K$, locally the cancellation of the two factors $N^{\otimes r}$ in the displayed formula. These identifications respect isomorphisms of $N$, tensor products of twists and base change. In particular every scalar automorphism $a\in\mathcal O_V^\times$ of $K$, acting by multiplication on every term, induces the identity on this pair. On a field-valued fibre, $\delta_K$ is nonzero exactly when that fibre of $K$ is acyclic.

source.place: Tags 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes) and 0FJY (remark-functorial-det), with more-algebra.tex Tag 0FJM (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes) and Section 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes). Degrees are reindexed from [-1,0] to [0,1]; the line-twist cancellation is the rank-zero exterior formula.

proof.text: Use sign-free reindexing $R(P)^i=P^{i+1}$, $d_{R(P)}^i=d_P^{i+1}$, and $R(f)^i=f^{i+1}$. Its inverse reindexes backwards; $H^i(R(P))=H^{i+1}(P)$, so both preserve quasi-isomorphisms and descend through the derived localization. This is not the usual signed differential of $P[1]$. Reindexing commutes with tensoring a module and with termwise pullback of a flat resolution. Thus $R(K)$ has Tor amplitude $[-1,0]$, and the window theorem supplies an affine open cover with finite locally free two-term models, refined to constant ranks. Fix the normalized derived pullback coherence supplied by the coherence theorem, and the affine cartesian determinant system supplied by the affine theorem. In Steps 2--8 we construct the global line and its arrows from this affine system; no previously chosen global determinant functor or its unspecified model comparisons are used.

source.place: Tags 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), 0FJY (remark-functorial-det), affine-local construction; sign-free reindexing written explicitly.

proof.text: For a model $P=[E^0\xrightarrow d E^1]$ of common rank $r$, use the explicit exterior line $L(P)=\det E^1\otimes(\det E^0)^\vee$. The top exterior map $\bigwedge^r d:\det E^0\to\det E^1$ defines its section $\delta_P$. On a free chart with ordered wedges $e=e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r$ and $f=f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge f_r$, write $\bigwedge^r d(e)=c f$ and set $\delta_P=c f\otimes e^\vee$. Changing $e$ by a unit $u$ multiplies $c$ by $u$ and $e^\vee$ by $u^{-1}$; changing $f$ by a unit $v$ multiplies $c$ by $v^{-1}$. This is the intrinsic top exterior map. The identification $\operatorname{Hom}(\det E^0,\det E^1)=L(P)$ and its inverse are evaluation on a generator and tensoring that image with its dual. These exterior lines are the displayed-model lines of the affine construction, with arrows given by its kernel-normalized good diagrams. Degree-zero exterior powers give $\delta_{[0\to0]}=1$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), exterior line and canonical element; Tag 0FJM (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), affine construction.

proof.text: Check preservation under a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to Q$ of affine finite projective two-term models (reindexed into degrees $-1,0$). The normalization theorem gives finite projective kernels $N^i$, an isomorphism $d_N$, and $T_a^{-1}(x)=\Gamma_a(x\otimes\delta_N)$. Take a common finite standard free cover of $N^{-1}$ and $Q^{-1},Q^0$; products of their covering elements still generate the unit ideal. The lifting property of the finite projective quotients gives sections of the two surjections; $x=(x-sa(x))+sa(x)$ gives the direct-sum splittings. The kernel-first wedge maps then give bases $(k,\widetilde q)$ in $P^{-1}$ and $(d_N k,\widetilde t)$ in $P^0$. In the wedge of their images under $d_P$, the kernel basis goes to $d_N k$. Every kernel component in an image $d_P\widetilde q$ wedges to zero against this full kernel wedge. The remaining quotient wedge is $\bigwedge d_Q(q)$. Therefore the kernel-first formula gives $\delta_P=\Gamma_a(\delta_Q\otimes\delta_N)$, so $T_a(\delta_P)=\delta_Q$. Scalar comparison identifies these localized formulas, including their duals and exact-sequence maps, with the original maps. Equality on the finite standard cover detects equality in the module. No invertibility of $d_P$ or $d_Q$ was used.

source.place: Tags 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), 0FJJ (lemma-canonical-element-well-defined); direct wedge argument filling the scope gap in the citation of 0FJC.

proof.text: The affine determinant theorem states that EVERY derived isomorphism acts by a kernel-normalized good-diagram map. For such an isomorphism $P\simeq Q$, write its map as $T_cT_b^{-1}$ for its good diagram $P\xleftarrow b M\xrightarrow c Q$. Both legs are surjective quasi-isomorphisms; their kernel differentials are isomorphisms by the normalization theorem. Their kernels have equal ranks in the two degrees, so if $P$ and $Q$ have rank zero, so does $M$. Step 3 gives $T_b\delta_M=\delta_P$ and $T_c\delta_M=\delta_Q$, hence $(T_cT_b^{-1})\delta_P=\delta_Q$. Independence of diagrams and the identity and composition laws are the affine determinant functor's existing assertions; we have only restricted its arrows to ones preserving the newly defined sections.

source.place: Tag 0FJM (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), good diagrams and passage to derived isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Write $s_P:B\otimes_A L(P)\to L(B\otimes_A P)$ for the explicit exterior scalar comparison, including duals and ordinary tensor symmetry. Its generator formula sends $1\otimes\delta_P$ to $\delta_{B\otimes_A P}$: the wedge of $d e_j$ goes to the wedge of $1\otimes d e_j$, and the dual basis goes to the dual basis. For a surjective quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to Q$, its termwise sequences split by projectivity as in Step 3. Tensor preserves these splittings, so its new kernel is $B\otimes_A N$ and its differential is still invertible. Compatibility of the exterior scalar maps with the kernel-first wedge maps, duals and evaluation gives
$$s_P(1\otimes\Gamma_a)(x\otimes\delta_N)=\Gamma_{B\otimes a}(s_Q(x)\otimes\delta_{B\otimes N}).$$
Substitute $T_a^{-1}(x)=\Gamma_a(x\otimes\delta_N)$ and cancel the isomorphisms. This proves $s_Q(1\otimes T_a)=T_{B\otimes a}s_P$. For $u$ represented by $P\xleftarrow b M\xrightarrow c Q$, the same equation for both legs and their inverses yields
$$s_Q(1\otimes T_u)=T_{Lu}\,s_P.$$
The tensor diagram is again good: its split kernel complexes remain contractible. The flat-complex and affine tensor comparison theorems identify it with the derived-pulled-back diagram, including for nonflat $A\to B$. The identity and associativity equations for these explicit $s$ are in the exterior scalar theorem; derived identifications use the fixed normalized coherence. Thus this equivariance applies to every further affine restriction, with no appeal to a global determinant comparison.

Choose affine model charts $(U_i,P_i,\alpha_i:P_i\simeq K|_{U_i})$. On an affine $W\subset U_i\cap U_j$, restrict both models via the exterior comparisons $s$. Define $g_{ij}$ there to be $T_{\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_i}:L(P_i)|_W\to L(P_j)|_W$. Step 5's equation makes these maps agree after further affine restriction. They therefore glue on the overlap: images of any local section agree on an affine cover, so the sheaf axiom gives its unique image; the inverse is obtained the same way. Step 4 gives $g_{ii}=1$, $g_{jk}g_{ij}=g_{ik}$ on affine triple-overlap charts and $g_{ij}\delta_{P_i}=\delta_{P_j}$, hence globally. Apply the sheaf-gluing theorem on the small site of opens of $V$, with this set-indexed cover. Concretely
$$D(K)(O)=\{(x_i)\in\prod_i L(P_i)(O\cap U_i):g_{ij}(x_i|)=x_j|\}.$$
Restriction, addition and scalar multiplication are componentwise. Linearity of $g_{ij}$ preserves the matching condition. Projection to the $i$th coordinate on $O\subset U_i$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $x\mapsto(g_{ij}(x|))_j$. Thus this is a module sheaf locally equal to $L(P_i)$, and is invertible. The matching tuple $(\delta_{P_i})_i$ is its global section $\delta_K$. All intersections are covered by affines, never assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), explicit affine gluing; sites.tex Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), underlying sheaf gluing.

proof.text:
For a derived isomorphism $u:K\simeq K'$, choose affine model charts $\alpha_i:P_i\simeq K$ and $\beta_j:Q_j\simeq K'$ and refine their overlaps by affines. Define the line map there as $T_{\beta_j^{-1}u\alpha_i}$. Step 5 makes it compatible with restrictions. On a change of source and target chart, affine composition gives
$$T_{\beta_{j'}^{-1}\beta_j}\,T_{\beta_j^{-1}u\alpha_i}
 =T_{\beta_{j'}^{-1}u\alpha_{i'}}\,T_{\alpha_{i'}^{-1}\alpha_i}.$$
It therefore defines a map of the matching-tuple sheaves in Step 6. Step 4 makes it section-preserving, and using $u^{-1}$ gives its inverse. The identity and composite equations follow on every affine chart from those for $T$. Taking $u=1_K$ between two choices of chart covers gives canonical inverse comparisons; for three choices their composites agree by the same equation. On any displayed model, comparison with the chosen charts is this very $T$, so the local formula holds for every model and is compatible with its derived isomorphisms. This constructs the functor on pairs and its model independence, with its local action specified rather than borrowed from an unrelated global functor.

source.place: Tag 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), gluing functoriality and canonical sections; affine arrows from more-algebra.tex Tag 0FJM.

proof.text:
Let $h:V'\to V$. Pullback preserves the two-term class by the window theorem. Cover $h^{-1}U_i$ by affine opens $W$; on $W$, the flat-complex pullback theorem and the affine tensor comparison identify $Lh^*P_i$ with the termwise scalar-extended model $h^*P_i$. Define the local line comparison $h^*L(P_i)\to L(h^*P_i)$ to be exactly $s_{P_i}$ of Step 5. On an overlap its equation
$$s_{P_j}\,h^*g_{ij}=g'_{ij}\,s_{P_i}$$
identifies the two local maps, where $g'_{ij}$ is the transition of the pulled-back models. These maps and their inverses glue to $h^*D(K)\simeq D(Lh^*K)$, using Step 7 to compare with any chosen target model charts. The generator equation in Step 5 proves section preservation. Naturality in derived isomorphisms is the same equivariance equation with $u$ in place of a transition. On three affine model charts, the two comparisons for a composite pullback are $s_{h^*P}h^*s_P$ and $s_P$ for the composite scalar extension, identified by the exterior associativity equation and the fixed normalized derived coherence. For an identity map the exterior comparison is the identity. Equality on affine covers proves all these diagrams globally, without a flatness assumption on $h$.

source.place: Tag 0FJY (remark-functorial-det), construction of the global pullback map from the exterior scalar maps and their equivariance.

proof.text: For a termwise isomorphism $u:P\to Q$, its kernel is zero. The kernel-first normalization formula therefore identifies its determinant action with $y\mapsto(\det u^1)y(\det u^0)^{-1}$, with the degrees now $0,1$. This follows directly from the zero-kernel exact-sequence wedge maps, with their empty kernel wedge equal to $1$. Apply this to multiplication by a unit $a$ on both terms of a rank-zero model of common rank $r$. Multilinearity gives $\bigwedge^r(a\,1)=a^r1$, so the action is $a^r a^{-r}=1$. The affine determinant theorem identifies this with the derived action, and Step 7 defines the global action by these very affine arrows, so the sheaf separatedness axiom extends the equality from model charts to $D(K)$. Thus every such scalar acts by the identity on the pair, even when $\delta_K=0$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), kernel-normalized comparison; Tag 0FJ9 (section-determinants), top exterior scalar action.

proof.text: Let $N$ be invertible. On an open where it has a generator $n$, the map $x\otimes n\mapsto x$ identifies $K\otimes N$ with $K$ in the derived category. Tensoring by $N$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms: locally this functor is the identity, so its cohomology maps are the same maps; in particular this is the ordinary and derived twist. Apply the functor on pairs already obtained to this local isomorphism. If $n'=a n$, the new map is $a^{-1}$ times the old map, and Step 9 says these induce the same map of determinant pairs. They consequently glue to a canonical isomorphism $(D(K\otimes N),\delta_{K\otimes N})\simeq(D(K),\delta_K)$; inverses glue as well. In a model, $\det(E^i\otimes N)\simeq\det E^i\otimes N^{\otimes r}$ sends the wedge of the $e_j\otimes n$ to $(\bigwedge e_j)\otimes n^{\otimes r}$. Cancelling the two $n^{\otimes r}$ factors gives exactly this glued map and preserves $\bigwedge^r d$. Changing the generator multiplies both factors by the same $a^r$.

source.place: Tag 0FJ9 (section-determinants), local exterior formula and rank-zero line-twist cancellation; agent-written extension of perfect.tex Tags 0FJX--0FJY.

proof.text: The twist comparisons are natural also in derived isomorphisms of $K$: with $n$ fixed, $\tau_n:K\otimes N\to K$ satisfies $u\tau_n=\tau_n(u\otimes1)$, and the functor on pairs preserves this equation. For an isomorphism $v:N\to N'$, choose generators $n,n'$ and write $v(n)=a n'$. The analogous square differs from the identity square by multiplication by $a$, whose determinant action is the identity by Step 9. For two twists, the generator $n\otimes m$ gives $\tau_{n\otimes m}=\tau_n\circ(\tau_m\text{ on the second twist})$ after the ordinary tensor associator. Functoriality gives precisely the required product and unit comparisons. Finally $h^*n$ generates $h^*N$, and the pullback of $\tau_n$ is $\tau_{h^*n}$. Naturality of the pair comparison in Step 8 gives the base-change square. All equations are local on the indicated trivializations and hence hold globally by sheaf separatedness.

source.place: Tag 0FJY (remark-functorial-det) and the preceding local-generator construction; agent-written coherence checks.

proof.text: On a field-valued fibre choose bases of its two vector spaces of common finite rank $r$. Base change in Step 8 identifies the section with $\det(d)$ times the displayed basis of the determinant line. Identify both vector spaces with the same $k^r$; the determinant-nonvanishing criterion for endomorphisms says that this coefficient is nonzero exactly when $d$ is bijective. The two-term cohomology is $\ker d$ in degree $0$ and $\operatorname{coker}d$ in degree $1$, so this is exactly acyclicity. For $r=0$ the differential of the zero object is an isomorphism and the empty determinant is $1$, consistent with this criterion. The argument also covers the empty scheme (unique sheaf data, no field-valued fibres), varying locally constant ranks, and characteristic two.
